q: A 2.0 m long steel bar of 20 mm diameter carries an axial tension of 50 kN. Taking E = 200 GPa, the elongation is closest to:
explain: A = π·20²/4 = 314.2 mm²; σ = 50 000/314.2 = 159.2 N/mm²; δ = σL/E = 159.2 × 2000 / 200 000 = 1.59 mm. 6.37 mm results from mixing up radius and diameter (A = πr²/4 = 78.5 mm²).

q: For a concrete mix with fixed cement content and aggregate grading, increasing the free water/cement ratio will most likely:
options: Increase workability and reduce strength and durability
Have no effect on strength provided curing is adequate
Increase both workability and long-term durability
explain: More free water increases slump/workability but raises capillary porosity in the hardened paste (Abrams' law), lowering strength and increasing permeability, hence reducing durability.

q: A prestressing strand is stretched and its ends are held at a fixed length. Over time the force in the strand reduces. This phenomenon is:
explain: Relaxation is loss of stress under constant strain. Creep is increase of strain under constant stress; creep rupture is failure under sustained stress; fatigue is damage under cyclic stress.

q: A higher carbon equivalent value (CEV) of a structural steel primarily indicates:
options: Better weldability and lower preheat requirement
Greater susceptibility to hydrogen cracking in the heat-affected zone
explain: CEV combines C, Mn, Cr, Mo, V, Ni, Cu content as a measure of hardenability. Higher CEV → harder, more brittle HAZ martensite → greater risk of hydrogen-induced cold cracking; more preheat is needed (EN 1011-2).

q: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 10 kN/m over the full span. The maximum bending moment is:
A 3 m cantilever carries a point load of 20 kN at its free end plus a UDL of 4 kN/m over its full length. The hogging moment at the fixed support is:
A solid circular shaft of 50 mm diameter transmits a torque of 1.5 kNm. The maximum shear stress is closest to:
A plane pin-jointed truss has 11 members, 7 joints and 3 independent reaction components, and is geometrically stable. It is:
explain: m + r = 11 + 3 = 14 = 2j = 14 → statically determinate (given stable geometry).

q: A beam fixed at both ends, span 5 m, carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. The fixed-end moment at each support is:
explain: FEM = wL²/12 = 12 × 5² / 12 = 25 kNm (37.5 kNm is the propped-cantilever value wL²/8).

q: At joint B, member BA (length 4 m, far end A fixed) and member BC (length 6 m, far end C pinned) meet. Both have the same EI. The distribution factor for BA is:
A fixed-ended beam of span 6 m with uniform plastic moment Mp = 120 kNm carries a central point load. The plastic collapse load is:
explain: Three hinges (two supports + midspan). Virtual work: P·(L/2)θ = Mp(θ + 2θ + θ) → P = 8Mp/L = 8 × 120/6 = 160 kN.

q: A vertical column 5 m tall is fixed at its base and completely free at the top. E = 210 GPa and I = 25 × 10⁶ mm⁴. The elastic critical (Euler) load is closest to:
explain: Fixed–free: L_cr = 2L = 10 m. N_cr = π²EI/L_cr² = π² × 210 000 × 25×10⁶ / 10 000² = 518 kN. 2073 kN results from wrongly using L_cr = L.

q: A soil has G_s = 2.70, void ratio e = 0.65 and water content w = 18%. Taking γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, its bulk unit weight is closest to:

A uniform deposit has γ = 18 kN/m³ above the water table and γ_sat = 20 kN/m³ below it. The water table is 2 m below ground. The vertical effective stress at 6 m depth is closest to (γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³):
A 6 m thick clay layer is drained at both top and bottom, with c_v = 2 m²/year. The time for 50% average consolidation (T_v = 0.197) is closest to:
explain: Double drainage → H_dr = 3 m. t = T_v H_dr²/c_v = 0.197 × 9/2 = 0.89 years. 3.55 years results from single drainage (H_dr = 6 m).

q: A vertical rectangular gate 2 m wide and 3 m high has its top edge at the free water surface. The resultant hydrostatic thrust on the gate is closest to (ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.81 m/s²):
explain: F = ρg h_c A = 1000 × 9.81 × 1.5 × (2 × 3) = 88.3 kN, acting at the centre of pressure 2.0 m below the surface (2/3 of the height).

q: Water (ρ = 1000 kg/m³) flows at 0.10 m³/s through a horizontal pipe that contracts from 300 mm to 150 mm diameter. Neglecting losses, the pressure drop across the contraction is closest to:
A 1:25 undistorted Froude-scaled model of a spillway passes 0.02 m³/s. The corresponding prototype discharge is:
According to Griffith theory, if the critical flaw length in a brittle material is increased fourfold, its fracture strength becomes:
explain: σ_f = √(2Eγ_s/πc) ∝ 1/√c. Four times the crack length → 1/√4 = ½ of the original strength.

q: A steel bar (ν = 0.30) is stretched to an axial strain of 0.001. The approximate unit volume change is:
explain: ΔV/V ≈ ε(1 − 2ν) = 0.001 × (1 − 0.6) = +4 × 10⁻⁴. Volume increases in tension for ν < 0.5 (the cross-sectional area shrinks, but less than the length grows).

q: A component cycles between a maximum stress of +150 MPa and a minimum of −50 MPa. The stress amplitude is:
explain: σ_a = (σ_max − σ_min)/2 = (150 − (−50))/2 = 100 MPa. Mean stress = 50 MPa; stress range = 200 MPa; R = σ_min/σ_max = −0.33.

q: A steel has C 0.18 %, Mn 1.20 %, Cr 0.10 %, Mo 0.05 %, V 0.02 %, Cu 0.15 %, Ni 0.10 %. Its carbon equivalent CE = C + Mn/6 + (Cr+Mo+V)/5 + (Cu+Ni)/15 is closest to:
A 1.20 m length of deformed reinforcing bar weighs 4.62 kg. Using A = M/(0.00785 L), its nominal diameter is:
Even at complete hydration, capillary pores remain in cement paste when the water/cement ratio exceeds about:
explain: Chemically combined water ≈ 0.20–0.24; with gel water, w/c ≈ 0.36–0.38 is needed to fill the space. Above that, capillary pores persist.

q: A mix has 450 kg/m³ OPC, 35 kg/m³ silica fume (efficiency factor k = 3) and 160 kg/m³ free water. The effective water/cement ratio for strength is closest to:

A 100 × 100 mm prism on a 300 mm span fails at 12 kN in four-point bending. Using f = Fl/(d₁d₂²), the flexural strength is:
A cement contains 0.25 % Na₂O and 0.60 % K₂O. Its equivalent alkali content and classification are:
explain: Na₂O_eq = 0.25 + 0.658 × 0.60 = 0.645 % > 0.60 % → not a low-alkali cement, so take extra ASR precautions with reactive aggregate.

q: Three coplanar concurrent forces act on a particle: 20 kN at 0°, 30 kN at 60° and 25 kN at 150° (angles from the +x axis). The magnitude of the resultant is closest to:
A force F = (2i − 3j + 6k) kN acts at the point r = (4i + 1j) m from O. The magnitude of its moment about O is closest to:
A vertical bar is fixed at top A and bottom B. Segment AC is 300 mm long with A = 300 mm²; segment CB is 300 mm long with A = 500 mm²; same E. A 400 kN downward load acts at C. The reaction at B is:
explain: Compatibility (δ_AC = δ_CB): R_A·L/A₁ = R_B·L/A₂ with R_A + R_B = 400. Flexibilities 1/300 : 1/500 → R_B = 400 × (1/300)/(1/300 + 1/500) = 250 kN (compression in CB); R_A = 150 kN.

q: A hollow circular shaft (outer Ø 100 mm, inner Ø 60 mm) transmits a torque of 10 kNm. The maximum shear stress is closest to:
explain: J = π(100⁴ − 60⁴)/32 = 8.55 × 10⁶ mm⁴; τ_max = Tc/J = 10 × 10⁶ × 50/8.55 × 10⁶ = 58.5 MPa. (50.9 MPa is a solid 100 mm shaft.)

q: A 50 mm solid steel shaft, 2 m long (G = 80 GPa), carries a torque of 1 kNm. The angle of twist is closest to:
A rectangular beam 100 mm wide × 300 mm deep carries a shear force of 60 kN. The maximum shear stress is:
explain: τ_max = 3V/(2A) = 1.5 × 60 000/(100 × 300) = 3.0 MPa, at the neutral axis.

q: A simply supported beam (span 6 m, EI = 20 000 kNm²) carries a central point load of 40 kN. Using moment-area, the end slope is:
explain: By symmetry the slope at midspan is zero; θ_A = area of M/EI from A to midspan = ½ × (L/2) × (PL/4)/EI = PL²/(16EI) = 40 × 36/(16 × 20 000) = 0.0045 rad.

q: A symmetric gable frame has 4 members and 5 joints, pinned at both bases (r = 4) with an internal hinge at the apex (c = 1). Using 3m + r vs 3j + c, the frame is:
explain: 3m + r = 12 + 4 = 16; 3j + c = 15 + 1 = 16 → equal → statically determinate (a three-pinned frame), given no geometric instability.

q: For a truss, real member forces N and unit-load forces n are: member 1 (N = +50 kN, n = +0.8, L = 4 m), member 2 (N = −30 kN, n = −0.6, L = 3 m), member 3 (N = +40 kN, n = 0, L = 5 m). AE = 200 000 kN for all. The deflection is:
A 5 m truss member (unit-load force n = 1.25) is heated by 30 °C (α = 12 × 10⁻⁶/°C). The contribution to the joint deflection is:
A simply supported beam spans 10 m. Using the influence line for bending moment at C (4 m from the left support), the moment at C due to a 5 kN/m UDL over the full span is:
A propped cantilever (fixed at A, propped at B), span 8 m, carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. By consistent deformation, the prop reaction is:
explain: Δ_B0 = wL⁴/8EI; f_BB = L³/3EI → R_B = 3wL/8 = 3 × 12 × 8/8 = 36 kN.

q: Member AB (L = 5 m, EI = 40 000 kNm²) is fixed at B, carries no span load and has no sway. Joint A rotates 0.002 rad clockwise. The end moment M_AB is:
explain: M_AB = (2EI/L)(2θ_A + θ_B − 3ψ) = (2 × 40 000/5)(2 × 0.002) = 64 kNm; and M_BA = 32 kNm (carry-over ½).

q: A truss member with EA/L = 50 MN/m is inclined at 30° to the global x-axis. The global stiffness term k₁₁ = (EA/L)λx² is:
A mercury U-tube manometer (SG 13.6) connected across two points in a water pipe at the same elevation shows a 200 mm deflection. The pressure difference is closest to:
explain: Δp = (ρ_Hg − ρ_w)g·h = (13.6 − 1) × 9810 × 0.2 = 24.7 kPa. (26.7 kPa ignores the water column above the mercury.)

q: A vertical rectangular gate, 2 m wide and 3 m high, has its top edge 1 m below the water surface. The depth of the centre of pressure is:
A quarter-circle gate of radius 2 m and width 3 m retains water on its concave side, with water level at the top of the gate. The vertical force component is closest to:
explain: F_V = weight of water above = ρg(πR²/4)w = 9.81 × π × 3 = 92.5 kN. F_H = ρg(R/2)(R·w) = 58.9 kN; resultant 109.6 kN.
